name: /about
description: Show Gemini CLI version information for diagnostics and issue reports.

examples.explanation: Display the installed Gemini CLI version.

when_to_use: Capture version details before filing a bug.

name: /agents
description: Manage discovered local and remote subagents, including listing, reloading, enabling, disabling, and configuring them.

examples.explanation: List all discovered built-in, local, and remote agents.

when_to_use: Inspect or change the subagents available to Gemini CLI.

conditions: Subagents remain a preview feature controlled by experimental.enableAgents.

name: /agents list
description: List all discovered agents, including built-in, local, and remote agents.

examples.explanation: Show every subagent currently registered with Gemini CLI.

when_to_use: Confirm that a subagent was discovered and is available.

conditions: Subagents remain a preview feature controlled by experimental.enableAgents.

name: /clear
description: Clear the active conversation context and terminal history, then start a new session.

examples.explanation: Start a new session with empty conversation context.

when_to_use: Begin an unrelated task with no prior conversation context.
when_not_to_use: Ctrl+L only redraws the terminal and does not clear conversation context.

name: /compress
description: Replace the chat context with a high-level summary to reduce token use in future turns.

examples.explanation: Summarize the current conversation before continuing.

when_to_use: Preserve the main thread of a long task while freeing context capacity.
when_not_to_use: Use /clear when you do not need any prior conversation context.

name: /resume
description: Browse and resume automatically saved sessions or manage project-scoped tagged checkpoints.

examples.explanation: Open the interactive browser for saved sessions.
Save a tagged checkpoint in the current project.

when_to_use: Continue a previous conversation or manage manual checkpoints.
when_not_to_use: Tagged checkpoints are project-scoped and are not visible from other project directories.

name: /model
description: Open model configuration or select a model, optionally persisting the choice.

examples.explanation: Select a model for the current session.

when_to_use: Inspect or change the model used by Gemini CLI.

name: /permissions
description: Manage folder trust and other Gemini CLI permissions.

examples.explanation: Open folder-trust management for the current directory.

when_to_use: Review or change whether a project directory is trusted.
when_not_to_use: Do not trust a directory whose contents you have not reviewed.

name: /plan
description: Switch to read-only Plan Mode and show the current plan when one exists.
when_to_use: Analyze and plan a change before allowing implementation.

conditions: Enabled by default; can be disabled with general.plan.enabled.

name: /mcp
description: List, inspect, authenticate, enable, disable, or reload configured Model Context Protocol servers.

examples.explanation: List configured MCP servers and their tools.

when_to_use: Inspect or change MCP server availability in the current session.

name: /skills
description: List, enable, disable, and reload Agent Skills discovered from supported locations.

examples.explanation: List discovered skills and whether each is enabled.

when_to_use: Inspect or change the reusable skills available to Gemini CLI.

description: Include text from a file or directory in the current prompt, using Git-aware filtering by default.

examples.explanation: Include README.md in a request to Gemini.
Include text files under src/ using the configured file filters.

when_to_use: Ground a prompt in specific local files or directories.
when_not_to_use: A lone @ is passed through as text and does not attach context.

conditions: Binary or very large files may be skipped or truncated.

description: Execute a shell command directly or toggle a persistent shell-input mode.

examples.explanation: Run git status and return to the Gemini CLI prompt.

when_to_use: Run a known shell command without asking the model to formulate it.
when_not_to_use: Shell commands have the same permissions and impact as commands run directly in the terminal.

conditions: Uses bash on Linux/macOS and PowerShell on Windows unless the Windows command processor is overridden.
